{"path":"snake_zai-glm-5.3-flash_01.html","edit_description":"Create a NEW complete self-contained single-file Snake game "snake_zai-glm-5.3-flash_01.html" (HTML + CSS + JS inline, zero dependencies, runs by double-clicking). Requirements:

PAGE/CSS:
- Dark neon theme, centered column layout: header with big title "SNAKE" and a HUD row; game stage with canvas + absolutely-positioned overlay div; footer with controls legend.
- HUD: left = "P1" score chip colored green, center = current mode label + status text, right = "P2" score chip colored orange; CPU players get a small "CPU" badge in their chip.
- Canvas 600x600 internal (30x30 grid, 20px cells), CSS responsive: width min(600px, 92vmin), aspect square.
- Overlay panels (menu / pause / game over) styled as centered glassy cards with backdrop blur over the canvas.

GAME RULES:
- Grid exactly 30x30. Tick loop: requestAnimationFrame + time accumulator, base tick 105ms, each food eaten globally reduces tick by 2ms down to minimum 60ms.
- Always 3 food items on the board; when eaten, respawn on a random free cell (not on any snake or other food). Eating grows snake by 1 segment and +1 point.
- A snake dies when its head hits a wall, its own body, the other snake's body, or head-to-head with the other snake's new head. Any death immediately ends the game.
- Two snakes: P1 green (#3ddc84) starting at (6,15) heading right; P2 orange (#ff9f1c) starting at (23,14) heading left; initial length 3.
- Winner logic: if exactly one snake survived the final tick, it wins; if both died the same tick, it's a draw ("Double KO").

MODES (start menu selects one):
1. "1 — Human vs Human": P1 controlled by Arrow keys, P2 by WASD.
2. "2 — CPU vs Human": P1 is CPU, P2 is human; when a mode has only ONE human snake, that snake accepts BOTH arrow keys and WASD.
3. "3 — CPU vs CPU": both snakes automatic.

CPU AI (decided each tick before movement, pure functions, no randomness except tie-break):
- BFS shortest path from snake head to the nearest food over free cells. Free = grid cell not occupied by any snake body EXCEPT each snake's tail cell (tail vacates this tick, approximation). Also block cells adjacent to the opponent's head (plus the head itself) to avoid head-on collisions; if BFS finds no path with that restriction, retry BFS without it.
- If a path exists, take the first step toward the food. Never allow reversing 180 degrees.
- If no path exists at all: survival move — among the 3 non-reversing directions, consider those that don't leave the board and don't hit a body cell; score each by flood-fill count of reachable free cells (penalize cells adjacent to opponent head by -1000), pick the best; if nothing is safe, keep current direction (will die).

INPUT:
- One keydown listener. Each human snake has a direction queue (max 2 pending); ignore 180° reversals relative to the snake's current direction.
- Global keys: in menu, 1/2/3 start the matching mode (menu buttons also clickable); during play P toggles pause, Esc aborts to menu; on game over R or Enter restarts the same mode, M or Esc returns to menu.
- Prevent default for arrows/space to avoid page scroll.

SCREENS:
- Start menu overlay: title, subtitle, three large mode buttons labeled with their number key and name, plus a compact controls legend (P1 arrows, P2 WASD, P pause).
- Pause overlay: "PAUSED" + "press P to resume".
- Game over overlay: winner announcement colored with winner's color (or "Draw — Double KO" in gray), final scores of both players, hints "R — restart • M — menu".

RENDERING (every frame):
- Board background #0e1116 with faint grid lines; foods as glowing red circles with a small white shine dot; snakes as rounded rectangles (use ctx.roundRect if available, fallback to fillRect with inset), body slightly darker toward tail, head brighter with two small white eye dots positioned by direction; draw dead snakes' final bodies too (game ends instantly anyway).

CODE STRUCTURE: clean sections with English comments: constants & helpers, state, reset/init per mode, input handling, CPU AI (bfsFirstStep, floodFillCount), tick logic (simultaneous movement with proper tail-vacate collision semantics: occupancy = bodies minus tails that move this tick, plus new heads; head-to-head same cell kills both), rendering, main loop, overlay/DOM helpers. No console errors, no external resources."}
